summary.tldr: Requires reporting on federal non-disclosure agreements, limits when public money can fund them, and sets rules for Parliament and federal bodies that use them.
what_it_does: Requires the President of the Treasury Board to table an annual report on non-disclosure agreements in the federal public sector, including how many were used and their total dollar value.

Bans federal officials who award grants and contributions from using public money to fund settlements for harassment, violence or discrimination if the settlement includes a non-disclosure agreement, or to fight complainants over non-disclosure agreements.
Requires organisations that receive federal grants or contributions to report each year to the President of the Treasury Board on their use of non-disclosure agreements.

Allows federal departments, Crown corporations, and some parliamentary bodies to use a non-disclosure agreement only if the complainant asks for it in writing, voluntarily, after having the chance to get independent legal advice.

Prohibits public money from being used to litigate non-disclosure agreements against complainants, and keeps certain disclosures allowed, including required disclosures, artistic expression, and communication with lawyers, health workers, and support people.
Requires Parliament to review the Act two years after it starts and every two years after that.
summary.background: The bill amends the Financial Administration Act and the Parliament of Canada Act. It also sets reporting rules for some entities whose financial information is included in the Public Accounts.
